title: Why Browsers Did Not Use C++

content.explanation: Browsers must safely execute code from unknown websites on millions of devices. C++ allows direct memory access, file access, and system-level operations. These capabilities are powerful but dangerous for the web. Browsers needed a lightweight language that was easy to learn, safe to run, and suitable for non-expert developers. JavaScript was designed specifically for these requirements.
content.example: A website should not be able to delete files from your computer through browser code.
content.analogy: Giving every visitor a master key to your house would be unsafe.
content.keyTakeaway: Browser languages prioritize safety over raw power.

revisionSummary: C++ was too powerful and unsafe.
